column1: # catalog/components.tsv — BH-6971 (BH-6546.1): every alert belongs to a component.
# One data row: component<TAB>regex<TAB>lane ids<TAB>log paths<TAB>owner doc. Exactly
# five tab-separated fields; write `-` for an empty one. A component may have
# more than one row (one regex per row). bin/component-of.sh matches the regex
# (POSIX ERE, bash [[ =~ ]]) against the alert line after a leading timestamp is
# removed, rows in FILE ORDER, and the first match wins. No match is `unowned`.
# A bad row stops the resolver (rc 2) with the line; `bin/component-of.sh --check`
# also checks that each lane id is catalog/lanes.d/<id>.json and the doc exists.
# A lane that writes through bin/lane-alert.sh shows as `[orchestrator/<lane>]`;
# its fallback path and most scripts write a bare `[<lane>]`. Both are matched.
# merge-conductor: bin/lib/mc/log.sh:289 `[merge-conductor] $text` (lane-alert.sh merge-conductor on the main path).
merge-conductor
